name: Turn a long script into a storyboard of video clips, one per scene (MartLLM)

assignments.name: script
assignments.value: Paste your script here. It can be a full voice-over, a blog post or a rough outline: the workflow cuts it into scenes and makes one clip for each.

assignments.name: look
assignments.value: Cinematic, realistic, soft natural light, the same color grade in every scene

assignments.name: scene_instructions
assignments.value:
You turn a script into a storyboard for a video model. You get the script, the most scenes allowed, the seconds each clip lasts, and the look.

Cut the script into scenes in order. Each scene covers one idea of the script. If the script has more ideas than scenes allowed, merge neighbours; never drop the ending.

For each scene write:
- text: the part of the script this scene covers, word for word where possible.
- video_prompt: ONE continuous shot a video model can make in that many seconds. Say the subject, the place, the light and how the camera moves, in plain concrete words. Describe recurring people and places the same way in every scene so the clips match. No on-screen text, no logos, no brand names, no real people.

Answer with JSON only: {"title": "a short title for the storyboard", "scenes": [{"text": "...", "video_prompt": "..."}]}

parameters.content:
## A storyboard of clips from a long script

Paste a script. A chat model cuts it into scenes and writes one shot for each. The workflow adds up the price of all clips first, then makes every clip at the same time and gives you a list: scene number, the script text, the clip link, the cost, and the clip file itself.

### Set up (2 minutes)
1. Get an API key at [martllm.com](https://martllm.com/go/n8n-script-storyboard) and add credit.
2. Open **Write the scene list** → Credential → Create new → **Header Auth**:
   - Name: `Authorization`
   - Value: `Bearer ` followed by your key
   Every MartLLM step uses this one credential.
3. Paste your script in **Settings** and click **Execute workflow**.

### What it costs
The workflow asks MartLLM for the price of every clip before any starts, and stops if the total is above `max_total_usd`. On 2026-11-25 the price list showed $0.039 per second at 480p and $0.085 per second at 720p for the default model, so six 5 second clips at 480p were about $1.18. The scene list costs a fraction of a cent. A clip that is not made costs nothing. Live prices: [martllm.com/models](https://martllm.com/models?type=video).

### Change it here
**Settings** holds the script, the most scenes, seconds per clip (5 to 15), the shape (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), 480p or 720p, sound on or off, the look every clip shares, the video model with a backup, and the most the whole run may cost.

### The total comes first
**Price each scene** asks what each exact clip costs; nothing is charged for asking. **Check the total** stops the run when the sum is above your limit, or shows MartLLM's own message if a request is refused.

### All clips at once
Every clip starts at the same time, so six clips take about as long as one: usually 1 to 5 minutes. The workflow checks every 20 seconds and stops waiting after 15 minutes. A clip that fails does not stop the others: it stays in the list with the reason.

### What you get
**Clip list** has one row per scene with the file attached in the `clip` field. The clip link needs your key and is kept about 3 hours, so to keep the clips add a Google Drive, S3 or YouTube step after **Clip list**. To join them into one film, use a video editor or ffmpeg.
